# TASK: BUILD "THE KEEPER'S LEDGER" — THE FLAGSHIP GAME
# Source: ALL_REMAINING_PLAN.md ITEM 4 (verbatim structure) + verified resources
# From: Runner (runner role: provide, verify — per Owner's operating model)

You are the 7-seat game-build roster, working as one crew:
- gamedesigner (LEAD — owns the build, the sequence, the delivery)
- game_director (vision, tone, what the game is about)
- game_level_content_designer (island arcs, keeper traces, event content)
- game_visual_direction (art direction, look, lighting mood)
- game_performance_engineer (frame budget, the 30fps reality on a T1000)
- game_balance_economist (the duty economy, storm difficulty curves)
- game_qa_critic (the 8.5 judgment — you are the gate)

========================================================================
## THE GAME — "THE KEEPER'S LEDGER"
========================================================================

THE PREMISE:
You are the last keeper of a lighthouse on a remote, storm-ravaged
island. Your light is the only thing keeping ships off the rocks —
and it is dying. The keepers before you vanished, one by one, and
nobody will say why. The supply boat stopped coming months ago.

THE LOOP:
Each night-cycle a storm rolls in, procedurally — different wind,
different rain, different fury. By day you work: feed the flame,
salvage parts from the wrecks that wash ashore, repair the lens
system, ration the oil, keep the log. Ships pass in the night. Some
see your beam and live. Some don't.

WHY THE PREVIOUS KEEPERS VANISHED — the story is not told to you,
it is CAUSED BY YOU:
The island keeps their traces — a ledger page, a rusted lantern, a
note in the lens room. Each keeper's record you find shows what they
neglected, and what it cost. The story advances on YOUR competence:
the lens you clean sets the beam's reach in fog; the oil you
rationed last week decides whether the light survives tonight; the
wreck you failed to report becomes the reef that sinks a ship later.
Neglect compounds. So does care.

THE ENDINGS BRANCH ON YOUR RECORD:
The game keeps an auditable log of every duty done or skipped —
your keeper record. The inspector who finally arrives reads it the
way the island does. Ships saved or sunk, storms ridden out or
suffered, the truth about the vanished keepers assembled or missed —
the ending you get is the one your record earned. No dialogue
choices. The job is the story.

THE ISLAND REMEMBERS:
Wrecks accumulate. Storm damage persists. Paths erode. New dangers
surface where past failures happened. The island permanently
changes — every playthrough's island tells the history of that
playthrough's keeper.

WHAT IT IS NOT: no combat, no enemy AI to build badly, no monsters.
The antagonist is the storm, the dark, and the sea — and your own
record.

========================================================================
## THE BAR — WHY THIS BEATS THE 8 GAMES ALREADY ON THE MARKET
========================================================================
(mined from real player reviews, re-verified Oct 17 with fresh web
research — the complaints below are VERIFIED with sources in the plan)

1. "Mechanics are decoration" — VERIFIED (Ironbark Lookout / Static
   Dread reviews: survival mechanics "completely pointless and affect
   nothing").
   -> YOUR FIX: every duty has mechanical weight. Lens = beam range;
   oil rationing = storm survival; reporting = future reefs. Nothing
   is decorative, and no purchasable item can switch the core loop off.

2. "Repetitive monotony" — VERIFIED ("dull monotony", "very very
   repetitive annoying running around").
   -> YOUR FIX: procedural storms + the remembering island mutate the
   loop every cycle; last cycle's failures physically change this
   cycle's job.

3. "Story makes no sense / tonally inconsistent / reveals too early"
   — VERIFIED ("the story made zero sense to me").
   -> YOUR FIX: the vanished-keepers mystery is assembled from records
   and from the player's own failures — the story emerges from the
   sim, so it cannot be inconsistent with it.

4. "Too short / anemic near the end" — VERIFIED ("falls off and feels
   anemic near the end").
   -> YOUR FIX: endings branch on the keeper record assembled across
   ALL cycles — the endgame is the payoff of the whole record, not a
   scripted cutscene.

5. "Cheap AI content breaks immersion" — VERIFIED ("soulless AI
   voice", "undisclosed GenAI", "AI artwork, sound effects").
   -> YOUR FIX: sound is synthesized (studio v3, real DSP), visuals
   are procedural code (no AI-image slop), and the zero-error bar
   (crash = failed build) is a gate, not a hope.

THE PRECEDENT THAT PROVES THE DESIGN:
Papers, Please — Lucas Pope, built alone, deliberately ugly, no
cinematics: sold beyond projection in a month, IGF Grand Prize,
BAFTA-nominated. The lesson the whole press repeated: "mechanics
carry the meaning... you live in the world your decisions produced."
THAT is the bar: the job produces the world, and the record decides
the ending. The keeper genre has the atmosphere and the audience —
but no game in it has made the job mechanically matter. That seat
is still empty. You are filling it.

========================================================================
## YOUR SEQUENCE (from the plan's full flow)
========================================================================

STEP 1 — UE5 VERIFY (already running):
A UE5.8.3 scalability test is in flight on the T1000 right now
(1080p, medium, volumetric fog + storms; PASS = >= 30fps on the test
scene). Its result decides your engine: PASS = Unreal; FAIL = Godot 4
stylized (documented decision). Check its outcome before Step 3.

STEP 2 — SPEC LOCK (your first work):
Write the full design doc BEFORE building anything: systems,
keeper-record mechanics, storm/lens/oil interactions, island layout,
endings, critic rubric. Brief-first law — the design exists on disk
before code does. FROM YOUR DESIGN, derive the complete asset list:
which character, which animations, which props. The plan's note
"Mixamo rig: walk/run/climb/row, provenance noted" is PROVISIONAL —
you decide what the design actually needs and where each asset comes
from. Provenance noted for every downloaded asset.

STEP 3 — BLENDER ASSET PHASE:
Drive Blender's Python API to build: procedural island + coastline,
lighthouse (exterior + interior), keeper character, boat, props,
storm sky. All original — no copyrighted assets. (Blender 5.2.2 at
C:/Users/agent/work/apps/blender-5.2.2-linux-x64/blender)

STEP 4 — UNREAL BUILD PHASE (or Godot, per Step 1's verdict):
Third-person controller, storm/weather system, the JOB-MATTERS
mechanics (lens -> beam range, oil rationing -> storm survival,
unreported wrecks -> future reefs), keeper-record auditable log,
save/load, menus, tutorial, settings. The 7 pblocks steer: director
(vision), level-content (arcs), visual (art), performance (frame
budget), balance (duty economy), qa-critic (the 8.5 judgment),
designer (lead).

STEP 5 — CRITIC LOOP:
Round = play the game -> screenshot from multiple viewpoints ->
your self-score AND qa-critic score -> binding = LOWER of the two ->
8.5+ = PASS; below = ranked issue list -> fixes -> re-round.
Up to 3 rounds (expect ~4h per iteration). Each round's scores +
issue list + diff logged. 3 rounds spent without 8.5 = honest
3-strikes report (scores, issues, what remains) — NO fake shipping.

STEP 6 — DELIVERY:
Playable build + scored screenshots + the keeper-record demo.
Everything committed. Status updated.

```python
import bpy, bmesh, math, random
from mathutils import noise, Vector

random.seed(1337)

def clear_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.cameras):
        for b in list(block):
            if b.users == 0:
                block.remove(b)

def mat(name, color, rough=0.9, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metal
    return m
```

Terrain with flat pad:
```python
def build_terrain():
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_grid_add(x_subdivisions=200, y_subdivisions=200, size=240)
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = "IslandTerrain"
    mesh = obj.data
    for v in mesh.vertices:
        x, y = v.co.x, v.co.y
        r = math.hypot(x, y)
        # island falloff: height high in middle, falls to below sea at r>70
        base = max(0.0, 1.0 - (r / 80.0)) ** 1.5
        n = noise.noise(Vector((x*0.05, y*0.05, 0.0)))  # -1..1-ish
        n2 = noise.noise(Vector((x*0.15, y*0.15, 7.3)))
        h = base * (6.0 + 4.0*n + 1.5*n2) - 1.2
        # flat pad for lighthouse near center
        if r < 9.0:
            h = 2.0
        elif r < 12.0:
            t = (r - 9.0) / 3.0
            h = 2.0 * (1 - t) + h * t
        v.co.z = h
```

{"content": "# Scalability test scene builder — The Keeper's Ledger (Step 1 verify)
# Builds: storm island terrain + ocean + lighthouse + props. Exports FBX for UE import.
# Run: blender -b -P build_scal_island.py
import bpy, math, random, os
from mathutils import noise, Vector

random.seed(1337)
OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "assets_blender")
OUT = os.path.abspath(OUT)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

def clear_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.cameras):
        for b in list(block):
            if b.users == 0:
                block.remove(b)

def mat(name, color, rough=0.9, metal=0.0, emit=0.0, emit_color=(1.0,0.75,0.4), glass=False):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name) or bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metal
    if emit > 0.0:
        for key in ("Emission Color", "Emission"):
            if key in bsdf.inputs:
                bsdf.inputs[key].default_value = (*emit_color, 1.0)
                break
        if "Emission Strength" in bsdf.inputs:
            bsdf.inputs["Emission Strength"].default_value = emit
    if glass:
        for key in ("Transmission Weight", "Transmission"):
            if key in bsdf.inputs:
                bsdf.inputs[key].default_value = 1.0
                break
        bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.05
    return m

def terrain_h(x, y):
    r = math.hypot(x, y)
    base = max(0.0, 1.0 - (r / 80.0)) ** 1.5
    n  = noise.noise(Vector((x * 0.05, y * 0.05, 0.0)))
    n2 = noise.noise(Vector((x * 0.15, y * 0.15, 7.3)))
    h = base * (6.0 + 4.0 * n + 1.5 * n2) - 1.2
    if r < 9.0:
        h = 2.0
    elif r < 12.0:
        t = (r - 9.0) / 3.0
        h = 2.0 * (1.0 - t) + h * t
    return h

def build_terrain():
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_grid_add(x_subdivisions=200, y_subdivisions=200, size=240)
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = "IslandTerrain"
    for v in obj.data.vertices:
        v.co.z = terrain_h(v.co.x, v.co.y)
    obj.data.materials.append(mat("M_Rock", (0.28, 0.27, 0.24), rough=0.95))
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    return obj

def build_ocean():
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=900, location=(0, 0, -0.6))
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = "Ocean"
    obj.data.materials.append(mat("M_Ocean", (0.02, 0.07, 0.10), rough=0.25))
    return obj

def build_lighthouse():
    parts = []
    def cyl(name, r1, r2, depth, z, material, verts=32):
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=verts, radius1=r1, radius2=r2,
                                            depth=depth, location=(0, 0, z))
        o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = name
        o.data.materials.append(material); parts.append(o); return o
    m_white = mat("M_TowerWhite", (0.75, 0.73, 0.68), rough=0.7)
    m_dark  = mat("M_TowerDark",  (0.10, 0.10, 0.11), rough=0.6)
    m_glass = mat("M_LampGlass",  (0.8, 0.85, 0.9), glass=True)
    m_lamp  = mat("M_LampCore",   (1.0, 0.85, 0.55), emit=8.0)
    cyl("LH_Base",    3.2, 3.2, 0.6, 2.3,  m_dark)
    cyl("LH_Tower",   2.6, 1.9, 16.0, 10.6, m_white)
    cyl("LH_Gallery", 2.7, 2.7, 0.35, 18.85, m_dark)
    cyl("LH_LampRoom",1.7, 1.7, 2.2, 20.2, m_glass)
    cyl("LH_LampCore",0.5, 0.5, 1.2, 20.2, m_lamp)
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=1.9, radius2=0.08, depth=1.4, location=(0, 0, 22.0))
    roof = bpy.context.active_object; roof.name = "LH_Roof"
    roof.data.materials.append(m_dark); parts.append(roof)
    return parts

def build_props():
    parts = []
    # keeper cottage
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(20, 10, 3.0))
    c = bpy.context.active_object; c.name = "CottageBody"; c.scale = (4.0, 2.8, 1.6)
    c.data.materials.append(mat("M_Wood", (0.35, 0.24, 0.15), rough=0.85)); parts.append(c)
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(20, 10, 4.4))
    r = bpy.context.active_object; r.name = "CottageRoof"; r.scale = (4.3, 3.1, 0.25)
    r.data.materials.append(mat("M_Roof", (0.15, 0.14, 0.13))); parts.append(r)
    # rocks
    m_rock = mat("M_Rock2", (0.22, 0.21, 0.20), rough=0.98)
    for i in range(25):
        ang = random.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
        rad = random.uniform(15, 68)
        x, y = rad * math.cos(ang), rad * math.sin(ang)
        s = random.uniform(0.8, 3.5)
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_ico_sphere_add(subdivisions=2, radius=s,
                                              location=(x, y, terrain_h(x, y) + s * 0.3))
        o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = f"Rock_{i:02d}"
        o.rotation_euler = (random.uniform(0, 3), random.uniform(0, 3), random.uniform(0, 3))
        o.data.materials.append(m_rock); parts.append(o)
    # pier: deck + posts, from shore toward sea at angle 40deg
    m_pier = mat("M_PierWood", (0.30, 0.22, 0.13), rough=0.9)
    ang = math.radians(40)
    for i in range(8):
        d = 58 + i * 2.4
        x, y = d * math.cos(ang), d * math.sin(ang)
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(x, y, 0.9))
        seg = bpy.context.active_object; seg.name = f"PierDeck_{i}"
        seg.scale = (2.6, 1.2, 0.08); seg.rotation_euler = (0, 0, ang)
        seg.data.materials.append(m_pier); parts.append(seg)
        if i % 2 == 0:
            for side in (-1, 1):
                px, py = x + side * math.sin(ang) * 1.1, y - side * math.cos(ang) * 1.1
                bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=0.09, depth=2.2, location=(px, py, 0.2))
                post = bpy.context.active_object; post.name = f"PierPost_{i}_{side}"
                post.data.materials.append(m_pier); parts.append(post)
    # wrecks (3 hulls)
    m_rust = mat("M_Rust", (0.30, 0.16, 0.08), rough=0.95, metal=0.4)
    for i, (wx, wy, wrot) in enumerate([(55, -25, 0.7), (-48, 30, 2.1), (-30, -52, 4.0)]):
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(wx, wy, 0.3))
        hull = bpy.context.active_object; hull.name = f"WreckHull_{i}"
        hull.scale = (5.0, 1.8, 1.0); hull.rotation_euler = (0.12, 0.05, wrot)
        hull.data.materials.append(m_rust); parts.append(hull)
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=0.08, depth=6.0,
                                            location=(wx, wy, 2.2),
                                            rotation=(math.radians(15), 0, wrot))
        mast = bpy.context.active_object; mast.name = f"WreckMast_{i}"
        mast.data.materials.append(m_pier); parts.append(mast)
    return parts

def export(path, objs):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for o in objs:
        o.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = objs[0]
    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath=path, use_selection=True, apply_unit_scale=True,
                             apply_scale_options='FBX_SCALE_NONE', object_types={'MESH'},
                             add_leaf_bones=False, bake_anim=False, mesh_smooth_type='OFF')
    print("[SCAL] exported", path, os.path.getsize(path), "bytes")

clear_scene()
terrain = build_terrain()
ocean = build_ocean()
lh = build_lighthouse()
props = build_props()
export(os.path.join(OUT, "env.fbx"), [terrain, ocean])
export(os.path.join(OUT, "lighthouse.fbx"), lh)
export(os.path.join(OUT, "props.fbx"), props)
print("[SCAL] DONE")
", "path": "tools/build_scal_island.py"}

{"content": "# UE5.8.3 headless editor script: import FBX, assemble storm island scene, save map.
# Run: UnrealEditor-Cmd ScalTest.uproject -run=pythonscript -script=<this file> -nullrhi
import unreal, os

ASSETS = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "assets_blender"))
TASK = unreal.AssetImportTask()
TASKS = []

def import_fbx(filename, dest):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.filename = os.path.join(ASSETS, filename)
    task.destination_path = "/Game/ScalContent/" + dest
    task.destination_name = dest
    task.automated = True
    task.save = True
    task.replace_existing = True
    TASKS.append(task)
    return task

import_fbx("env.fbx", "SM_Env")
import_fbx("lighthouse.fbx", "SM_Lighthouse")
import_fbx("props.fbx", "SM_Props")
unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks(TASKS)
unreal.log("[SCAL] imports done")

def mesh(path):
    return unreal.load_asset(path) if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path) else None

sm_env = mesh("/Game/ScalContent/SM_Env")
sm_lh = mesh("/Game/ScalContent/SM_Lighthouse")
sm_props = mesh("/Game/ScalContent/SM_Props")
unreal.log("[SCAL] assets: env=%s lh=%s props=%s" % (sm_env is not None, sm_lh is not None, sm_props is not None))

# --- new empty level ---
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.new_level("/Game/Lvl_ScalStorm")

def spawn(cls, name, loc, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
    a = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(cls, unreal.Vector(*loc), unreal.Rotator(*rot))
    if a:
        a.set_actor_label(name)
    return a

# environment meshes
for sm, z in ((sm_env, 0.0), (sm_lh, 0.0), (sm_props, 0.0)):
    if sm:
        a = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_object(sm, unreal.Vector(0, 0, z))
        a.set_actor_label("Env_" + sm.get_name())

# storm lighting
sun = spawn(unreal.DirectionalLight, "StormSun", (0, 0, 500), (-35, 140, 0))
if sun:
    sun.set_mobility(unreal.Mobility.STATIONARY)
    comp = sun.get_editor_property("root_component")
    comp.set_editor_property("intensity", 0.6)
    comp.set_editor_property("light_source_angle", 8.0)
    comp.set_editor_property("use_temperature", True)
    comp.set_editor_property("temperature", 7500.0)

skylight = spawn(unreal.SkyLight, "StormSky", (0, 0, 300))
if skylight:
    comp = skylight.get_editor_property("root_component")
    try:
        comp.set_editor_property("real_time_capture", True)
    except Exception as e:
        unreal.log("[SCAL] skylight realtime: %s" % e)

fog = spawn(unreal.ExponentialHeightFog, "StormFog", (0, 0, 0))
if fog:
    comp = fog.get_editor_property("component")
    setv = False
    for prop in ("b_enable_volumetric_fog", "enable_volumetric_fog", "bEnableVolumetricFog"):
        try:
            comp.set_editor_property(prop, True)
            setv = True
            break
        except Exception:
            pass
    for prop, val in (("fog_density", 0.06), ("fog_max_opacity", 0.9)):
        try:
            comp.set_editor_property(prop, val)
        except Exception:
            pass
    unreal.log("[SCAL] volumetric fog set=%s" % setv)

try:
    clouds = spawn(unreal.VolumetricCloud, "StormClouds", (0, 0, 0))
    unreal.log("[SCAL] clouds spawned=%s" % (clouds is not None))
except Exception as e:
    unreal.log("[SCAL] clouds failed: %s" % e)

atmo = spawn(unreal.SkyAtmosphere, "StormAtmosphere", (0, 0, 0))

pp = spawn(unreal.PostProcessVolume, "StormPP", (0, 0, 0))
if pp:
    pp.set_editor_property("unbound", True)

spawn(unreal.PlayerStart, "PlayerStart", (0, 45, 6), (0, 180, 0))

ctrl = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_editor_world()
unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_map(ctrl, "/Game/Lvl_ScalStorm")
unreal.log("[SCAL] map saved")
print("[SCAL] BUILD DONE")

{"content": "# UE5.8.3 headless editor script: import FBX, assemble storm island scene, save map.
# Run: UnrealEditor-Cmd ScalTest.uproject -run=pythonscript -script=<this file> -nullrhi
# Writes a build report to logs/scene_build.txt (stdout capture is unreliable).
import unreal, os

BASE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".."))
ASSETS = os.path.join(BASE, "assets_blender")
REPORT = os.path.join(BASE, "logs", "scene_build.txt")
rep_lines = []

def note(msg):
    rep_lines.append(msg)
    unreal.log("[SCAL] %s" % msg)

# --- imports (idempotent: replace_existing) ---
TASKS = []
def import_fbx(filename, dest):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.filename = os.path.join(ASSETS, filename)
    task.destination_path = "/Game/ScalContent/" + dest
    task.destination_name = dest
    task.automated = True
    task.save = True
    task.replace_existing = True
    TASKS.append(task)

import_fbx("env.fbx", "SM_Env")
import_fbx("lighthouse.fbx", "SM_Lighthouse")
import_fbx("props.fbx", "SM_Props")
unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks(TASKS)
note("imports done")

def meshes_under(folder):
    out = []
    for a in unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.list_assets(folder, recursive=True):
        obj = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(a)
        if obj and obj.get_class().get_name() == "StaticMesh":
            out.append(obj)
    return out

env_meshes = meshes_under("/Game/ScalContent/SM_Env")
lh_meshes = meshes_under("/Game/ScalContent/SM_Lighthouse")
prop_meshes = meshes_under("/Game/ScalContent/SM_Props")
note("meshes env=%d lh=%d props=%d" % (len(env_meshes), len(lh_meshes), len(prop_meshes)))

# --- level (idempotent) ---
map_path = "/Game/Lvl_ScalStorm"
try:
    unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.new_level(map_path)
except Exception as e:
    note("new_level failed (%s), loading existing" % e)
    unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.load_level(map_path)

def spawn(cls, name, loc, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
    a = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(cls, unreal.Vector(*loc), unreal.Rotator(*rot))
    if a:
        a.set_actor_label(name)
    return a

def set_prop(obj, prop, val):
    try:
        obj.set_editor_property(prop, val)
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        note("prop %s failed: %s" % (prop, e))
        return False

# --- environment meshes ---
spawned = 0
for sm in env_meshes + lh_meshes + prop_meshes:
    a = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_object(sm, unreal.Vector(0, 0, 0))
    if a:
        a.set_actor_label("Env_" + sm.get_name())
        spawned += 1
note("mesh actors spawned=%d" % spawned)

# --- storm lighting ---
sun = spawn(unreal.DirectionalLight, "StormSun", (0, 0, 500), (-35, 140, 0))
if sun:
    comp = sun.get_editor_property("root_component")
    set_prop(comp, "intensity", 0.6)
    set_prop(comp, "light_source_angle", 8.0)
    set_prop(comp, "use_temperature", True)
    set_prop(comp, "temperature", 7500.0)

skylight = spawn(unreal.SkyLight, "StormSky", (0, 0, 300))
if skylight:
    comp = skylight.get_editor_property("root_component")
    if not set_prop(comp, "real_time_capture", True):
        set_prop(comp, "bRealTimeCapture", True)

fog = spawn(unreal.ExponentialHeightFog, "StormFog", (0, 0, 0))
if fog:
    comp = fog.get_editor_property("component")
    setv = set_prop(comp, "b_enable_volumetric_fog", True)
    if not setv:
        setv = set_prop(comp, "bEnableVolumetricFog", True)
    set_prop(comp, "fog_density", 0.06)
    set_prop(comp, "fog_max_opacity", 0.9)
    note("volumetric fog set=%s" % setv)

try:
    clouds = spawn(unreal.VolumetricCloud, "StormClouds", (0, 0, 0))
    note("clouds spawned=%s" % (clouds is not None))
except Exception as e:
    note("clouds failed: %s" % e)

spawn(unreal.SkyAtmosphere, "StormAtmosphere", (0, 0, 0))

pp = spawn(unreal.PostProcessVolume, "StormPP", (0, 0, 0))
if pp:
    set_prop(pp, "unbound", True)

spawn(unreal.PlayerStart, "PlayerStart", (0, 45, 6), (0, 180, 0))

ctrl = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_editor_world()
unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_map(ctrl, map_path)
note("map saved")

with open(REPORT, "w") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(rep_lines) + "\n")
note("BUILD DONE")

Still 0 spawned even with the subsystem. The lights/clouds/fog spawn fine (they're classes), but `spawn_actor_from_object` with a StaticMesh asset fails. Why?

Hypothesis: in a commandlet world, spawning from an object may require the world to be an editor world with a world context... but class spawning works. The difference: spawn_actor_from_object needs to create an actor from an asset — maybe it needs the mesh to be loaded/valid, or maybe it fails because the map is "unsaved new level" state...

Alternative approach that's known-robust: use `unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset` then create a `StaticMeshActor` via `actor_sub.spawn_actor_from_class(unreal.StaticMeshActor, ...)` and set its static mesh component's `static_mesh` property. That's the classic pattern:

```python
a = sub.spawn_actor_from_class(unreal.StaticMeshActor, loc, rot)
comp = a.get_editor_property("static_mesh_component")  # or root_component
comp.set_static_mesh(sm, unreal.MeshComponentStaticLightingInfo?) 
```

Actually the standard call: `static_mesh_component.set_static_mesh(mesh)` — in UE python: `comp.set_static_mesh(sm)` exists on StaticMeshComponent (SetStaticMesh). Let me use that. There's also `a.set_actor_scale3d` etc.

Another possibility for the failure: spawn_actor_from_object signature is (asset, location, rotation, scale?) — maybe it requires a non-None rotation parameter or the asset must be a Blueprint class, not a raw mesh. Docs: `spawn_actor_from_object(asset, location, rotation=..., ...)` — "Spawn Actor from Object: Spawn an actor with the specified asset (this will only work with assets that can be spawned like blueprints or static meshes)". Should work... but in commandlet maybe the asset-to-actor factory path needs the asset registry fully loaded.

Rather than fight it, use StaticMeshActor + set_static_mesh — deterministic and well-documented. Also note: the map saved BEFORE (7 actors) — lights spawn fine via class path.

Also I should double check `set_static_mesh` signature in 5.8: `StaticMeshComponent.set_static_mesh(new_mesh, new_collision_info?)` — older versions: `set_static_mesh(new_mesh)` returns bool. There's also `unreal.StaticMeshComponent.set_static_mesh(mesh)` — I'll try with try/except and a second variant with collision info.

# THE KEEPER'S LEDGER — DESIGN DOC (SPEC LOCK v1.0)

## 1. VISION (game_director)
One line: "The job is the story." You are the last keeper. The light is dying. Your record decides everything.
Pillars:
1. Every duty has mechanical weight (no decoration)
2. The island remembers (persistent consequence)
3. The record is the story (no dialogue choices; auditable log → endings)
4. Storm is the antagonist (procedural, readable, fair)
Tone: quiet dread, competence fantasy, melancholy. Papers Please precedent: mechanics carry meaning.
Name promise check [76c0c46d67f3]: "The Keeper's Ledger" promises: a keeper's job + a ledger that matters. The build delivers exactly: keeper duties + auditable ledger + record-based endings. No feature creep beyond this doc [5666e7d38315: one owner per decision].

## 2. CORE LOOP (gamedesigner)
Day phase (work): 
- Read the night's report (what the beam did, what ships passed, what failed)
- Duties: feed flame/oil, clean lens, repair mechanisms, salvage wrecks, log entries, report wrecks to the ledger/chart
- Explore island: traces of previous keepers (ledger pages, notes, lanterns)
Night phase (storm): 
- Storm rolls procedurally (wind, rain, fog density, duration, fury 1-5)
- The beam runs on oil you loaded, lens clarity you set, mechanisms you repaired
- Ships spawn on lanes; their fate resolves against your beam's actual reach/reliability
- You can intervene at night: adjust flame, trim wick, restart mechanism if it fails (tension events)
Dawn: results post to the ledger. Ships saved/sunk. Damage persists. New wrecks may wash ashore (which you should salvage AND report).

Cycle = one day+night, target 12-18 min real time. 12 cycles = full run (~3h) + endings.

## 3. THE JOB-MATTERS SYSTEMS (the anti-decoration law)
Each duty maps to a mechanical effect. NOTHING is cosmetic:

### 3.1 OIL ECONOMY (balance seat)
- Oil is the single survival resource. Sources: salvage from wrecks (barrels), reserve cache (finite, island-wide), boat deliveries (stopped — story beat).
- Flame burn rate = f(flame height setting). Higher flame = more reach but more burn.
- Rationing: you set daily ration; the lamp room tank holds X hours at current burn.
- Night survival: if oil hits 0 mid-storm → beam dies → ships in fog are lost → record marks "dark interval".
- Tradeoff: burn bright (save ships, drain oil) vs ration (risk dark intervals). No dominant strategy: storm fury distribution punishes both pure strategies [0b5d7f574911].

### 3.2 LENS SYSTEM (the beam's reach)
- Lens clarity 0-100%: salt crust, soot, cracks. Cleaning restores clarity (day work, consumes cloth/agent? no — time only).
- Lens alignment: mechanism wear shifts alignment; repair restores.
- Beam reach in clear = base; in fog = base * clarity * alignment factor. Fog is the storm's main weapon, so lens work directly = ships saved.
- Cracked lens (if neglected too long) = permanent reach penalty until repaired with salvaged lens parts (from wrecks).

### 3.3 MECHANISM (rotation + wick feed)
- The lens rotates (flash characteristic). Mechanism wear → rotation stalls → beam becomes steady (less noticeable in rain) → ships misjudge.
- Wick feed jams → flame dips → dark intervals even with oil.
- Repair with salvaged gears/clockwork from wrecks.

### 3.4 WRECKS → REEFS (the remembering island)
- Storms wash wrecks ashore (hull sections, cargo, barrels, bodies of ships that sank because of unlit coasts).
- Each wreck must be: salvaged (parts+oil) AND reported (logged in the wreck ledger + marked on the chart).
- Unreported wreck = unmarked hazard → future storms push it into a reef position → later ships hit it. The island literally accumulates your neglect as new reefs.
- Reported wrecks get buoy markers (crafted from salvage) — visible, and they prevent reef formation.
- Cap: island holds max 6 wreck sites; each unreported one raises future storm's ship-loss chance.

### 3.5 THE KEEPER RECORD (auditable log — the story spine)
- Every duty done/skipped posts an entry: timestamped, categorized (LAMP / LENS / MECHANISM / WRECKS / LOG / ISLAND).
- The record is a real data structure, serialized to save file, viewable in-game as the ledger book UI.
- Entries are facts, not judgments: "Night 4: dark interval 47 min. 2 ships unaccounted."
- The INSPECTOR (endgame) reads the record and derives the ending. Also: traces of previous keepers reference THEIR records — each vanished keeper's trace shows a neglected duty category, and the pattern of their fates mirrors what neglect costs. Assembling all 5 traces + your own record = the truth about why they vanished (they each broke under the same job; the island/sea took them when their records failed — no supernatural cop-out, the horror is the job).
- Story-emerges-from-sim guarantee: trace texts are written to reference duty categories and consequences, never contradicting player state. The mystery cannot be inconsistent because it's assembled from the same data that drives mechanics.

### 3.6 SHIPS (the score)
- Ships spawn on 2-3 lanes per night, count scales with storm fury and cycle.
- Each ship resolves: sees beam (reach/fog/flash characteristic) → holds safe course; doesn't → risk roll vs hazards (rocks, unreported reefs, wreck drift).
- Outcomes: PASSED / TURNED AWAY (safe, but no trade credit) / WRECKED (visible: distress flare, wreck washes ashore next day).
- You never talk to ships. Flares and bells are the only voice. (No dialogue choices — the job is the story.)

## 4. STORM SYSTEM (procedural)
- Parameters: fury 1-5, wind dir/speed, rain density, fog density, duration, gust events, lightning.
- Seeded per cycle: seed = run_seed + cycle. Deterministic per run (reproducible for QA).
- Fury curve across 12 cycles: ramp with breather valleys [bb3570f4e15b escalation-breather ramp]: e.g. 1,2,2,3,2,3,4,3,5,4,5,5 — tuned by balance seat.
- Storm damage: gusts above threshold damage mechanism/lens/gallery glass; damage persists until repaired (island remembers).
- Lightning: occasional flash lights (cheap: point light flash + thunder audio) — no volumetric clouds (budget law).

## 1. VISION (game_director seat)

**One line: The job is the story.**

You are the last keeper of a storm-ravaged island lighthouse. The keepers before you
vanished, one by one. The supply boat stopped coming. Every night a storm tests the
light; every day the island shows you what last night cost — and what the keepers
before you left behind.

Pillars (in priority order — when in doubt, cut toward the top):
1. **Every duty has mechanical weight.** Nothing is decorative. If a duty doesn't
   change a number that matters, it doesn't ship.
2. **The island remembers.** Wrecks, damage, erosion, reefs — the island is the
   history of your playthrough, physically.
3. **The record is the story.** No dialogue choices. An auditable log of duties done
   and skipped decides what the inspector reads and which ending you earn.
4. **The storm is the antagonist.** Procedural, readable, fair. It has tells. It
   never cheats.

Tone: quiet dread + competence fantasy. The Papers, Please precedent: mechanics carry
the meaning; you live in the world your decisions produced.

Name-promise check [game_director:76c0c46d67f3]: "The Keeper's Ledger" promises a
keeper's job AND a ledger that matters. The build delivers exactly these two things.
Feature creep is the enemy; anything not in this doc is out of scope.

## 2. CORE LOOP (gamedesigner seat)

**Cycle = one Day + one Night. Target 12–18 real minutes. A full run = 12 cycles + ending (~3h).**

### DAY (work phase)
1. **Read the night's report** at the log desk: what the beam did, which ships passed
   or were lost, what failed, what washed ashore.
2. **Duties** (each maps to mechanics — see section 3):
   - Load oil / set the ration
   - Clean the lens (clarity), repair the mechanism (rotation + wick feed)
   - Salvage wrecks on Wreck Shore (parts, oil)
   - Report wrecks at the chart house (marks them on the chart, prevents reefs)
   - Maintain paths (drainage) where storms eroded them
   - Keep the log (write the day's entry — feeds the record's completeness)
3. **Explore** for the five traces of the previous keepers (optional, story-critical).
4. **Light the lamp at dusk.** The night then runs on what you actually loaded, set,
   cleaned, and repaired. No take-backs.

### NIGHT (storm phase)
- A procedural storm rolls in (section 4). The beam runs autonomously from your day's work.
- You may move through the tower at night: trim the wick, nudge the ration, restart a
  stalled mechanism — physical interventions under time pressure, not menus.
- Ships spawn on lanes and resolve against your beam's real reach, the real fog, and
  the real hazard map (including reefs your unreported wrecks became).
- Outcomes post to the ledger at dawn: PASSED / TURNED AWAY / WRECKED.

### DAWN
Results post. Damage persists. New wrecks may have washed ashore. Autosave (diegetic:
"the log is written"). The island shows its memory.

## 3. THE JOB-MATTERS SYSTEMS (anti-decoration law — the heart of the game)

### 3.1 OIL ECONOMY (game_balance_economist seat)
- Oil is the single survival resource. Sources: salvage from wrecks (barrels), a finite
  island reserve in the shed, no resupply (the boat is gone — that's the story).
- **Burn rate = f(flame height).** You set flame height: higher = longer reach, more burn.
- **Ration:** you set the night's ration at the tank. Tank capacity is finite; the
  ration decides how long the light holds.
- **Dark interval:** if oil hits zero mid-storm, the beam dies for as long as the oil
  stays at zero. Every ship in fog during a dark interval is at maximum risk. The
  record logs the interval to the minute.
- Tradeoff: burn bright (save ships, drain reserve) vs ration (risk dark intervals).
  Storm fury is random enough that neither pure strategy dominates [game_balance_economist:0b5d7f574911].

### 3.2 LENS → BEAM REACH
- **Clarity 0–100%:** salt crust and soot accumulate daily; cleaning restores it.
  Clarity multiplies effective reach, and fog is the storm's main weapon — so lens
  work is literally ships-saved.
- **Alignment:** mechanism wear degrades alignment; repair restores it.
- **Cracks:** neglect clarity below 20% for two nights and the lens cracks — a
  permanent reach penalty until repaired with lens parts salvaged from wrecks.

### 3.3 MECHANISM (rotation + wick feed)
- The lens assembly rotates; the flash characteristic is how ships identify the light.
  Wear → rotation stalls → steady beam → ships misread it in rain.
- Wick feed jams → flame dips → dark intervals even with oil in the tank.
- Both repaired with clockwork/gears salvaged from wrecks. Wear is visible (wobble,
  tick irregularity — audio tells before failure).

### 3.4 WRECKS → REEFS (the remembering island)
- Storms wash wrecks ashore (hull sections, cargo, oil barrels, sometimes a crew's
  belongings — story material).
- Each wreck must be **salvaged** (parts + oil) AND **reported** at the chart house.
- **Unreported wreck = unmarked hazard.** Later storms push it off the shore into the

  accumulates your neglect as new dangers on the map.
- Reported wrecks get a buoy (built from salvage) — marked, safe, visible.
- Island holds max 6 wreck sites. Each unreported one raises ship-loss odds in every
  later storm. This is the game's memory made physical.

  LAMP / LENS / MECHANISM / WRECKS / LOG / ISLAND.
- Entries are **facts, not judgments**: "Night 4: dark interval 47 min. 2 ships unaccounted."

- **The inspector reads it** at the end (section 6). The ending is arithmetic on the
  record — no hidden flags, no dialogue.
- **The five traces** (previous keepers) each show THEIR record fragment: what they
  neglected, what it cost. The mystery assembles from records — yours and theirs.
  The truth: each keeper broke under the same job; the sea took them when their
  records failed. No monsters. The horror is the ledger.
- **Story-emerges-from-sim guarantee:** trace texts reference duty categories and
  consequences, never player-specific state they can't know — so the story cannot
  contradict the sim, because it is made of the sim's own data.

- Resolution per ship: sees the beam (reach × clarity × alignment vs fog) → holds a

- Outcomes: PASSED / TURNED AWAY (safe, no credit) / WRECKED (distress flare at night;
  the wreck washes ashore next day — and waits for your report).
- You never talk to ships. Flares, bells, and the beam are the only voices.

## 4. STORM SYSTEM (procedural)
- Parameters: fury 1–5, wind direction/speed, rain density, fog density, duration,
  gust events, lightning strikes.
- **Seeded:** storm seed = run_seed + cycle → deterministic per run (reproducible for

One island, five regions, walkable end-to-end in ~4–6 minutes. No fast travel (the
walk is short and the island IS the game).

1. **Lighthouse Point** (center-south, high ground): the tower — lamp room (lens,

Cycle 13, dawn: the inspector's boat finally arrives. They walk the island and read
the ledger. The ending is **derived arithmetic on the record**:

Inputs: ships_saved, ships_lost, dark_interval_minutes, wrecks_reported/unreported,

- Save contains: full world state, keeper record, island memory (wrecks/reefs/erosion),
  storm seed state, cycle counter. Loading restores exactly.
- Autosave at every dawn + manual save at the log desk. Single slot + backup.

- **Ships:** 2–5 per night by fury. Base loss odds 12% in fury-3 fog with healthy beam;

{"content": "# THE KEEPER'S LEDGER — full game environment (Step 3)
# Island (5 regions per SPEC_LOCK 5), lighthouse ext+int, all props.
# Run: blender -b -P build_game_env.py
import bpy, math, os, random
from mathutils import noise, Vector

random.seed(20261020)
OUT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "assets_blender"))
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
REPORT = []

def note(m): REPORT.append(m); print("[ENV]", m)

def clear_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.cameras):
        for b in list(block):
            if b.users == 0: block.remove(b)

_mcache = {}
def mat(name, color, rough=0.9, metal=0.0, emit=0.0, emit_color=(1.0,0.75,0.4), glass=False):
    key = name
    if key in _mcache: return _mcache[key]
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    b = m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    b.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = rough
    b.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metal
    if emit > 0:
        for k in ("Emission Color", "Emission"):
            if k in b.inputs: b.inputs[k].default_value = (*emit_color, 1.0); break
        if "Emission Strength" in b.inputs: b.inputs["Emission Strength"].default_value = emit
    if glass:
        for k in ("Transmission Weight", "Transmission"):
            if k in b.inputs: b.inputs[k].default_value = 1.0; break
        b.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.05
    _mcache[key] = m
    return m

def cyl(name, r, depth, loc, material, verts=24, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=verts, radius=r, depth=depth, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = name; o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def cone(name, r1, r2, depth, loc, material, verts=24, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(vertices=verts, radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = name; o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def cube(name, size, loc, material, scale=(1,1,1), rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=size, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = name; o.scale = scale
    o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def sphere(name, r, loc, material, subdiv=2):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_ico_sphere_add(subdivisions=subdiv, radius=r, location=loc)
    o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = name; o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

# ============ TERRAIN: 5 regions (SPEC_LOCK 5) ============
# Lighthouse Point center-south high; Cottage Row east; Wreck Shore west;
# Old Landing north (pier+chart house); Back Hills south.
def terrain_h(x, y):
    r = math.hypot(x, y)
    base = max(0.0, 1.0 - (r / 110.0)) ** 1.4
    n  = noise.noise(Vector((x*0.045, y*0.045, 0.0)))
    n2 = noise.noise(Vector((x*0.14,  y*0.14,  7.3)))
    n3 = noise.noise(Vector((x*0.30,  y*0.30,  13.1)))
    h = base * (7.0 + 4.5*n + 1.6*n2 + 0.5*n3) - 1.4
    # Lighthouse Point: hill at (0,-20) up to 8m
    d = math.hypot(x-0, y+20)
    h += max(0.0, 1.0 - d/26.0)**2 * 6.0
    if d < 7.0: h = 8.0  # tower pad
    # Back Hills: rolling south
    d2 = math.hypot(x-10, y+55)
    h += max(0.0, 1.0 - d2/40.0)**1.5 * 3.5
    # Cottage Row: gentle shelf east
    d3 = math.hypot(x-38, y-8)
    h = max(h, (max(0.0, 1.0-d3/22.0)**1.2 * 3.2) + 0.4)
    # Wreck Shore: low west beach
    d4 = math.hypot(x+45, y-5)
    h -= max(0.0, 1.0-d4/30.0)**1.3 * 2.2
    # Old Landing: flat north pier area
    d5 = math.hypot(x-5, y-52)
    h = max(h, (max(0.0, 1.0-d5/20.0)**1.1 * 2.2) + 0.2)
    # path smoothing along main route (lighthouse->landing->cottage->shore)
    for (px,py,pr) in [(0,-12,3.5),(0,0,3.5),(2,18,3.5),(4,36,3.5),(5,50,3.5),
                       (14,-6,3.0),(28,-7,3.0),(38,-8,3.0),
                       (-16,-8,3.0),(-32,-6,3.0),(-45,-5,3.0),
                       (6,-34,2.8),(9,-46,2.8)]:
        dp = math.hypot(x-px, y-py)
        if dp < pr:
            t = dp/pr
            h = h*(t) + (h+0.15)*(1-t)  # slightly raised, smoothed
    return h

def build_terrain():
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_grid_add(x_subdivisions=220, y_subdivisions=220, size=300)
    o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = "IslandTerrain"
    for v in o.data.vertices:
        v.co.z = terrain_h(v.co.x, v.co.y)
    o.data.materials.append(mat("M_Ground", (0.23,0.24,0.18), rough=0.95))
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    note("terrain done")
    return o

def build_ocean():
    o = cube("Ocean", 1, (0,0,-0.9), mat("M_Ocean", (0.02,0.06,0.09), rough=0.2), scale=(700,700,0.5))
    return o

# ============ LIGHTHOUSE (ext + int) ============
def build_lighthouse():
    parts = []
    m_white = mat("M_TowerWhite", (0.72,0.70,0.66), rough=0.65)
    m_dark  = mat("M_TowerDark", (0.09,0.09,0.10), rough=0.6)
    m_glass = mat("M_LampGlass", (0.75,0.82,0.88), glass=True)
    m_lamp  = mat("M_LampCore", (1.0,0.82,0.5), emit=10.0)
    m_brass = mat("M_Brass", (0.65,0.5,0.25), rough=0.35, metal=0.8)
    m_wood  = mat("M_Wood", (0.32,0.22,0.13), rough=0.85)
    m_stone = mat("M_Stone", (0.30,0.29,0.27), rough=0.95)
    # exterior
    parts.append(cyl("LH_Base", 3.4, 0.8, (0,-20,8.4), m_stone))
    parts.append(cone("LH_Tower", 2.7, 2.0, 15.0, (0,-20,16.3), m_white))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_Gallery", 2.9, 0.35, (0,-20,24.0), m_dark))
    for i in range(14):  # gallery railing
        a = i/14.0*2*math.pi
        parts.append(cyl(f"LH_Rail_{i}", 0.045, 1.0, (2.75*math.cos(a), -20+2.75*math.sin(a), 24.7), m_dark, verts=8))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_LampRoom", 1.8, 2.4, (0,-20,25.4), m_glass, verts=32))
    for i in range(8):  # glazing bars
        a = i/8.0*2*math.pi
        parts.append(cyl(f"LH_Bar_{i}", 0.05, 2.4, (1.75*math.cos(a), -20+1.75*math.sin(a), 25.4), m_dark, verts=8))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_LampCore", 0.55, 1.3, (0,-20,25.3), m_lamp, verts=16))
    parts.append(cone("LH_Roof", 1.95, 0.06, 1.5, (0,-20,27.3), m_dark))
    # door
    parts.append(cube("LH_Door", 1, (0,-17.35,9.3), m_wood, scale=(1.1,0.15,2.2)))
    # interior: spiral stair + landings (inside tower, y=-20)
    z = 9.0
    step_i = 0
    while z < 23.6:
        a = step_i * 0.42
        r_in = 0.9
        x = r_in*math.cos(a); y = -20 + r_in*math.sin(a)
        s = cube(f"LH_Step_{step_i}", 1, (x,y,z), m_wood, scale=(0.85,0.32,0.06), rot=(0,0,a))
        parts.append(s)
        z += 0.31; step_i += 1
    note("stair steps=%d" % step_i)
    # landings at 3 heights (keeper room, mid, lamp)
    parts.append(cyl("LH_Floor_Keeper", 2.4, 0.25, (0,-20,12.6), m_wood, verts=32))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_Floor_Mid", 2.3, 0.22, (0,-20,18.4), m_wood, verts=32))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_Floor_Lamp", 1.9, 0.3, (0,-20,24.2), m_wood, verts=32))
    # keeper room furniture (on 12.6 floor)
    parts.append(cube("LH_LogDesk", 1, (1.2,-21.6,13.35), m_wood, scale=(1.5,0.8,0.1)))
    for dx in (-0.9,0.9):
        parts.append(cyl(f"LH_DeskLeg_{dx}", 0.06, 0.75, (1.2+dx,-21.6,12.97), m_wood, verts=8))
    parts.append(cube("LH_Bed", 1, (-1.3,-18.8,13.15), m_wood, scale=(1.1,2.2,0.35)))
    parts.append(cube("LH_BedMattress", 1, (-1.3,-18.8,13.45), mat("M_Cloth",(0.45,0.42,0.36)), scale=(1.0,2.0,0.22)))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_OilTank", 0.75, 1.5, (1.6,-18.6,13.6), m_brass, verts=20))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_TankGauge", 0.09, 0.06, (1.6,-17.82,13.9), mat("M_Gauge",(0.85,0.83,0.75),emit=0.4), verts=12, rot=(math.pi/2,0,0)))
    # lens assembly (lamp floor 24.2): pedestal + lens drum
    parts.append(cyl("LH_LensPedestal", 0.5, 0.9, (0,-20,24.8), m_brass, verts=16))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_LensDrum", 0.95, 1.5, (0,-20,25.7), m_glass, verts=32))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_LensCore", 0.4, 1.1, (0,-20,25.7), m_lamp, verts=16))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_LensRing_Top", 1.0, 0.08, (0,-20,26.5), m_brass, verts=32))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_LensRing_Bot", 1.0, 0.08, (0,-20,24.95), m_brass, verts=32))
    # wick mechanism + clockwork (visible wear target)
    parts.append(cyl("LH_Clockwork", 0.35, 0.5, (0.8,-20.9,24.75), m_brass, verts=16))
    parts.append(cyl("LH_WickFeed", 0.12, 0.8, (0.45,-20.45,25.2), m_brass, verts=10, rot=(0,math.pi/2.6,0)))
    note("lighthouse done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

# ============ BUILDINGS ============
def build_buildings():
    parts = []
    m_wood  = mat("M_Wood", (0.32,0.22,0.13), rough=0.85)
    m_wood2 = mat("M_WoodDark", (0.22,0.15,0.09), rough=0.9)
    m_roof  = mat("M_Roof", (0.14,0.13,0.12), rough=0.8)
    m_stone = mat("M_Stone", (0.30,0.29,0.27), rough=0.95)
    # Cottage (Cottage Row east, at ~(38,-8), terrain ~3.2)
    cx, cy, cz = 38, -8, terrain_h(cx,cy)
    parts.append(cube("Cottage_Body", 1, (cx,cy,cz+1.5), m_wood, scale=(4.2,3.0,1.5)))
    parts.append(cone("Cottage_Roof", 3.6, 0.1, 1.6, (cx,cy,cz+3.05), m_roof, verts=4, rot=(0,0,math.pi/4)))
    parts.append(cube("Cottage_Door", 1, (cx,cy-3.02,cz+1.1), m_wood2, scale=(0.9,0.1,2.0)))
    parts.append(cube("Cottage_Window", 1, (cx-2.0,cy-3.02,cz+1.6), mat("M_WindowGlass",(0.6,0.7,0.75),emit=0.8), scale=(1.0,0.08,0.9)))
    parts.append(cyl("Cottage_Chimney", 0.35, 1.8, (cx+1.4,cy+0.8,cz+3.6), m_stone, verts=12))
    # Supply shed
    sx, sy = 33, -2
    sz = terrain_h(sx,sy)
    parts.append(cube("Shed_Body", 1, (sx,sy,sz+1.0), m_wood2, scale=(2.2,1.8,1.0)))
    parts.append(cone("Shed_Roof", 1.9, 0.08, 0.7, (sx,sy,sz+1.85), m_roof, verts=4, rot=(0,0,math.pi/4)))
    parts.append(cube("Shed_Door", 1, (sx,sy-1.82,sz+0.8), m_wood, scale=(0.8,0.08,1.5)))
    # Chart house (Old Landing north, ~(8,48))
    hx, hy = 8, 48
    hz = terrain_h(hx,hy)
    parts.append(cube("ChartHouse_Body", 1, (hx,hy,hz+1.4), m_wood, scale=(3.2,2.4,1.4)))
    parts.append(cone("ChartHouse_Roof", 2.8, 0.1, 1.2, (hx,hy,hz+2.7), m_roof, verts=4, rot=(0,0,math.pi/4)))
    parts.append(cube("ChartHouse_Door", 1, (hx,hy-2.42,hz+1.0), m_wood2, scale=(0.9,0.1,1.9)))
    parts.append(cube("ChartHouse_Window", 1, (hx+1.6,hy-2.42,hz+1.5), mat("M_WindowGlass",(0.6,0.7,0.75),emit=0.8), scale=(0.9,0.08,0.8)))
    # chart table inside (visible through door)
    parts.append(cube("ChartHouse_Table", 1, (hx,hy+0.3,hz+0.85), m_wood2, scale=(1.8,0.9,0.08)))
    # Signal post (cottage row)
    px, py = 36, -14
    pz = terrain_h(px,py)
    parts.append(cyl("SignalPost", 0.09, 4.5, (px,py,pz+2.25), m_wood2, verts=10))
    parts.append(cube("SignalYard", 1, (px,py,pz+4.2), m_wood2, scale=(1.4,0.08,0.08)))
    # Salvage bench (Wreck Shore west)
    bx, by = -42, -3
    bz = terrain_h(bx,by)
    parts.append(cube("SalvageBench_Top", 1, (bx,by,bz+0.85), m_wood, scale=(2.0,0.9,0.09)))
    for dx in (-0.8,0.8):
        parts.append(cyl(f"SalvageBench_Leg_{dx}", 0.07, 0.8, (bx+dx,by,bz+0.42), m_wood2, verts=8))
    parts.append(cube("SalvageBench_Vise", 1, (bx+0.7,by,bz+1.0), mat("M_Iron",(0.2,0.2,0.22),rough=0.5,metal=0.7), scale=(0.25,0.3,0.3)))
    note("buildings done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

# ============ PIER (Old Landing) ============
def build_pier():
    parts = []
    m_pier = mat("M_PierWood", (0.28,0.20,0.12), rough=0.9)
    ang = math.radians(188)  # pointing north-ish into sea from landing
    x0, y0 = 5, 56
    for i in range(14):
        d = i * 2.2
        x = x0 + d*math.cos(ang); y = y0 + d*math.sin(ang)
        z = 1.1 if i < 10 else 1.1
        parts.append(cube(f"Pier_Deck_{i}", 1, (x,y,z), m_pier, scale=(2.4,2.3,0.09), rot=(0,0,ang)))
        if i % 2 == 0:
            for side in (-1,1):
                ox = side*math.sin(ang)*1.05; oy = -side*math.cos(ang)*1.05
                parts.append(cyl(f"Pier_Post_{i}_{side}", 0.09, 2.4, (x+ox,y+oy,z-1.1), m_pier, verts=8))
    # boat moored at pier end
    bx = x0 + 30*math.cos(ang); by = y0 + 30*math.sin(ang)
    parts.append(cube("MooringPost", 1, (x0+28*math.cos(ang), y0+28*math.sin(ang), 1.5), mat("M_Iron",(0.2,0.2,0.22),metal=0.7), scale=(0.15,0.15,0.8)))
    note("pier done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts, (bx, by)

# ============ ROCKS / CLIFFS / DRIFTWOOD ============
def build_nature():
    parts = []
    m_rock = mat("M_Rock", (0.21,0.20,0.19), rough=0.98)
    m_rock2 = mat("M_RockWet", (0.16,0.16,0.16), rough=0.75)
    m_wood = mat("M_Driftwood", (0.35,0.28,0.20), rough=0.95)
    # cliff ring rocks + scattered
    for i in range(60):
        a = random.uniform(0, 2*math.pi)
        rad = random.uniform(20, 95)
        x, y = rad*math.cos(a), rad*math.sin(a)
        if terrain_h(x,y) < -0.5:  # only in water/shore
            s = random.uniform(1.0, 4.5)
            parts.append(sphere(f"Rock_{i:02d}", s, (x,y,terrain_h(x,y)+s*0.25), m_rock2 if terrain_h(x,y)<0 else m_rock))
    for i in range(30):
        a = random.uniform(0, 2*math.pi)
        rad = random.uniform(14, 80)
        x, y = rad*math.cos(a), rad*math.sin(a)
        h = terrain_h(x,y)
        if h > 0.2:
            s = random.uniform(0.5, 2.2)
            parts.append(sphere(f"RockIn_{i:02d}", s, (x,y,h+s*0.3), m_rock))
    # driftwood on wreck shore
    for i in range(12):
        x = random.uniform(-52,-34); y = random.uniform(-16,10)
        h = terrain_h(x,y)
        if h > 0.1:
            parts.append(cube(f"Driftwood_{i:02d}", 1, (x,y,h+0.12), m_wood, scale=(random.uniform(1.5,3.5),0.18,0.14), rot=(0,random.uniform(-0.1,0.1),random.uniform(0,3.1))))
    note("nature done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

# ============ WRECKS (3 initial hulls, Wreck Shore) ============
def build_wrecks():
    parts = []
    m_rust = mat("M_Rust", (0.28,0.15,0.07), rough=0.95, metal=0.4)
    m_wood = mat("M_WoodWet", (0.24,0.17,0.10), rough=0.9)
    for i,(wx,wy,wrot) in enumerate([(-48,-14,0.7),(-44,4,2.4),(-52,-2,4.1)]):
        h = terrain_h(wx,wy)
        parts.append(cube(f"Wreck_Hull_{i}", 1, (wx,wy,h+0.5), m_wood if i%2 else m_rust, scale=(4.5,1.7,0.9), rot=(0.10,0.04,wrot)))
        parts.append(cube(f"Wreck_Rib_{i}_a", 1, (wx-1.2,wy,h+1.1), m_wood, scale=(0.15,1.5,0.7), rot=(0,0,wrot)))
        parts.append(cube(f"Wreck_Rib_{i}_b", 1, (wx+1.2,wy,h+1.0), m_wood, scale=(0.15,1.4,0.5), rot=(0,0,wrot)))
        parts.append(cyl(f"Wreck_Mast_{i}", 0.09, 5.5, (wx,wy,h+2.4), m_wood, verts=8, rot=(math.radians(18),0,wrot)))
    note("wrecks done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

# ============ BACK HILLS TRACE SITES (5 markers, subtle) ============
def build_trace_sites():
    parts = []
    m_rust = mat("M_RustOld", (0.30,0.18,0.09), rough=0.95, metal=0.3)
    m_cloth = mat("M_ClothOld", (0.4,0.36,0.30), rough=0.95)
    sites = [(14,-38,"Trace_Lantern"), (2,-52,"Trace_Ledger"), (22,-50,"Trace_Note"),
             (-6,-44,"Trace_Lantern2"), (10,-60,"Trace_Boots")]
    for i,(x,y,nm) in enumerate(sites):
        h = terrain_h(x,y)
        if nm.endswith("Lantern") or nm.endswith("Lantern2"):
            parts.append(cyl(nm, 0.16, 0.42, (x,y,h+0.21), m_rust, verts=10))
            parts.append(cyl(nm+"_Glass", 0.11, 0.22, (x,y,h+0.30), mat("M_LanternGlass",(0.8,0.7,0.45),emit=0.25), verts=10))
        elif nm == "Trace_Ledger":
            parts.append(cube(nm, 1, (x,y,h+0.06), m_cloth, scale=(0.42,0.30,0.09), rot=(0,0,0.4)))
        elif nm == "Trace_Note":
            parts.append(cube(nm, 1, (x,y,h+0.02), mat("M_Paper",(0.75,0.72,0.62)), scale=(0.30,0.22,0.015), rot=(0,0,1.2)))
        else:
            for dx in (-0.12,0.12):
                parts.append(cube(nm+f"_{dx}", 1, (x+dx,y,h+0.10), m_cloth, scale=(0.14,0.30,0.18)))
    note("trace sites done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

# ============ PATH MARKERS (erosion system anchors, subtle stones) ============
def build_pathstones():
    parts = []
    m_stone = mat("M_PathStone", (0.34,0.33,0.30), rough=0.95)
    route = [(0,-12),(0,0),(2,18),(4,36),(5,50),(14,-6),(28,-7),(38,-8),(-16,-8),(-32,-6),(-45,-5),(6,-34),(9,-46)]
    for i,(x,y) in enumerate(route):
        h = terrain_h(x,y)
        for j in range(3):
            ox, oy = random.uniform(-2,2), random.uniform(-2,2)
            parts.append(sphere(f"PathStone_{i}_{j}", random.uniform(0.15,0.3), (x+ox,y+oy,terrain_h(x+ox,y+oy)+0.08), m_stone, subdiv=1))
    note("pathstones done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

def export(path, objs):

import bpy, math, os

    b.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*color, 1.0)

    b.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metal

            if k in b.inputs: b.inputs[k].default_value = (1.0,0.8,0.5,1.0); break
        if "Emission Strength" in b.inputs: b.inputs["Emission Strength"].default_value = emit
    return m

def cyl(name, r, depth, loc, material, verts=16, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=verts, radius=r, depth=depth, location=loc, rotation=rot)

    return o

def cube(name, size, loc, material, scale=(1,1,1), rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=size, location=loc, rotation=rot)

    return o

def sphere(name, r, loc, material, subdiv=3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_ico_sphere_add(subdivisions=subdiv, radius=r, location=loc)
    o = bpy.context.active_object; o.name = name; o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

# ============ KEEPER (stylized, readable silhouette — oilskin + hat) ============
def build_keeper():
    parts = []
    m_oilskin = mat("M_Oilskin", (0.13,0.16,0.15), rough=0.55)   # dark yellow-green slicker
    m_oilhat  = mat("M_OilHat",  (0.16,0.19,0.17), rough=0.5)
    m_boots   = mat("M_Boots",   (0.08,0.07,0.06), rough=0.6)
    m_skin    = mat("M_Skin",    (0.55,0.42,0.33), rough=0.7)
    m_lantern = mat("M_Lantern", (0.5,0.4,0.2), rough=0.4, metal=0.6)
    m_wick    = mat("M_WickGlow",(1.0,0.75,0.4), emit=3.0)
    # proportions: total ~1.8m, origin at feet
    # legs
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_LegL", 1, (-0.11,0,0.42), m_oilskin, scale=(0.13,0.15,0.42)))
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_LegR", 1, (0.11,0,0.42), m_oilskin, scale=(0.13,0.15,0.42)))
    # boots
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_BootL", 1, (-0.11,0.03,0.10), m_boots, scale=(0.15,0.24,0.10)))
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_BootR", 1, (0.11,0.03,0.10), m_boots, scale=(0.15,0.24,0.10)))
    # torso (oilskin coat)
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_Torso", 1, (0,0,1.05), m_oilskin, scale=(0.34,0.22,0.42)))
    # coat skirt
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_CoatSkirt", 1, (0,0,0.78), m_oilskin, scale=(0.36,0.24,0.14)))
    # arms
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_ArmL", 1, (-0.24,0,1.02), m_oilskin, scale=(0.10,0.12,0.38)))
    parts.append(cube("Keeper_ArmR", 1, (0.24,0,1.02), m_oilskin, scale=(0.10,0.12,0.38)))
    # hands
    parts.append(sphere("Keeper_HandL", 0.07, (-0.24,0,0.80), m_skin, subdiv=2))
    parts.append(sphere("Keeper_HandR", 0.07, (0.24,0,0.80), m_skin, subdiv=2))
    # head + sou'wester hat
    parts.append(sphere("Keeper_Head", 0.14, (0,0,1.42), m_skin, subdiv=3))
    parts.append(cone("Keeper_Hat", 0.17, 0.05, 0.12, (0,0,1.53), m_oilhat, verts=12))
    parts.append(cyl("Keeper_HatBrim", 0.20, 0.03, (0,0,1.48), m_oilhat, verts=12))
    # lantern in right hand (the keeper's signature prop)
    parts.append(cyl("Keeper_LanternBody", 0.06, 0.12, (0.24,0,0.70), m_lantern, verts=10))
    parts.append(cyl("Keeper_LanternFlame", 0.025, 0.05, (0.24,0,0.70), m_wick, verts=8))
    parts.append(cyl("Keeper_LanternRing", 0.045, 0.015, (0.24,0,0.78), m_lantern, verts=10))
    note("keeper done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

# ============ SUPPLY BOAT (the boat that stopped coming — story prop at pier) ============
def build_boat():
    parts = []
    m_hull = mat("M_BoatHull", (0.18,0.22,0.24), rough=0.6)
    m_deck = mat("M_BoatDeck", (0.35,0.28,0.20), rough=0.85)
    m_cabin= mat("M_BoatCabin",(0.25,0.28,0.30), rough=0.7)
    m_glass= mat("M_BoatGlass",(0.6,0.7,0.75), rough=0.2)
    # hull: tapered box via scaled cubes (stylized)
    parts.append(cube("Boat_HullBase", 1, (0,0,0.35), m_hull, scale=(1.1,3.2,0.5)))
    parts.append(cube("Boat_Bow", 1, (0,3.0,0.45), m_hull, scale=(0.7,1.2,0.4), rot=(0,0,0)))
    parts.append(cube("Boat_Stern", 1, (0,-3.0,0.45), m_hull, scale=(0.9,0.8,0.4)))
    parts.append(cube("Boat_GunwaleL", 1, (-1.05,0,0.75), m_hull, scale=(0.12,6.2,0.35)))
    parts.append(cube("Boat_GunwaleR", 1, (1.05,0,0.75), m_hull, scale=(0.12,6.2,0.35)))
    parts.append(cube("Boat_Deck", 1, (0,0,0.62), m_deck, scale=(1.9,5.8,0.06)))
    # cabin
    parts.append(cube("Boat_Cabin", 1, (0,-1.6,1.05), m_cabin, scale=(1.3,1.6,0.7)))
    parts.append(cube("Boat_CabinGlass", 1, (0,-0.78,1.15), m_glass, scale=(1.1,0.06,0.4)))
    # mast + boom (cargo crane feel)

    parts.append(cyl("Boat_Boom", 0.05, 2.2, (0,2.4,1.5), m_cabin, verts=8, rot=(math.radians(55),0,0))
    # mooring rope hint
    parts.append(cyl("Boat_Cleat", 0.05, 0.3, (1.0,2.2,0.85), m_cabin, verts=8, rot=(0,math.pi/2,0)))
    note("boat done (%d parts)" % len(parts))
    return parts

keeper = build_keeper()
boat = build_boat()

def export(path, objs):

{"content": "# Probe UE 5.8.3 Python API capabilities for the game architecture decision
import unreal, os
out = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "logs", "api_probe.txt"))
lines = []

def probe(label, fn):
    try:
        v = fn()
        lines.append("%s = %s" % (label, v))
    except Exception as e:
        lines.append("%s FAILED: %s" % (label, e))

# 1. BlueprintEditorLibrary capabilities
import unreal.BlueprintEditorLibrary as bel
probe("bel attrs", lambda: [a for a in dir(bel) if not a.startswith('_')][:40])

# 2. DataTable creation from CSV (for content: traces, storms, endings)
probe("DataTableFactory", lambda: hasattr(unreal, 'DataTableFactory'))
probe("CSVImportFactory", lambda: hasattr(unreal, 'CSVImportFactory'))

# 3. SaveGame class
probe("SaveGameObject", lambda: hasattr(unreal, 'SaveGameObject'))

# 4. GameplayStatics core
probe("GMS attrs", lambda: [a for a in dir(unreal.GameplayStatics) if 'save' in a.lower() or 'open' in a.lower()][:10])

# 5. Input: key polling from Python?
probe("SysLib input", lambda: [a for a in dir(unreal.SystemLibrary) if 'input' in a.lower() or 'key' in a.lower()][:10])

# 6. ExecutePythonCommand ex (for thin-BP hybrid)
probe("PythonBPLib", lambda: hasattr(unreal, 'PythonScriptLibrary'))
if hasattr(unreal, 'PythonScriptLibrary'):
    probe("pylib attrs", lambda: [a for a in dir(unreal.PythonScriptLibrary) if not a.startswith('_')][:10])

# 7. Spawn + actor factories
probe("ActorFactory", lambda: hasattr(unreal, 'ActorFactory'))
probe("BPFactory", lambda: hasattr(unreal, 'BlueprintFactory'))

# 8. Enhanced Input classes
probe("EnhancedInput", lambda: [a for a in dir(unreal) if 'EnhancedInput' in a or 'InputMapping' in a][:8])

# 9. Widget/UI creation from Python
probe("WidgetBlueprint", lambda: hasattr(unreal, 'WidgetBlueprintFactory'))
probe("WidgetBlueprintLibrary", lambda: [a for a in dir(unreal.WidgetBlueprintLibrary) if not a.startswith('_')][:12] if hasattr(unreal, 'WidgetBlueprintLibrary') else 'N/A')

# 10. Level streaming + world composition (for island regions)
probe("LevelStreaming", lambda: [a for a in dir(unreal) if 'LevelStreaming' in a][:6])

with open(out, "w") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
", "path": "tools/ue_api_probe.py"}
